content: To plant a garden is to believe in tomorrow.
author: Audrey Hepburn
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Living in pretense takes an enormous amount of mental energy. When you constantly manage impressions to please others, you end up feeling like an imposter in your own skin.

In Audrey Hepburn's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Honesty with yourself can feel uncomfortable at first, but it is the only ground upon which a real life can be built. When you stop lying to yourself about your feelings, your energy is immediately freed up.
reflectionPrompt: If genuine peace is not dependent on future achievements, how can you celebrate being alive today?
